nodes.content: Investigate embodied grounding of action verbs that transfers across robot morphologies while distinguishing intended effects from observed motions.
requirements: Achieve ≥70% instruction success on unseen morphologies when motion cues conflict with intended effects.
Distinguish identical motions producing different effects while recognizing different motions achieving the same instructed effect.

nodes.content: Train EffectBind using contrastive same-motion/different-effect and cross-morphology different-motion/same-effect rollouts to learn morphology-invariant verb embeddings for goal-conditioned control.
On unseen grippers, can EffectBind distinguish sliding from rotation when identical wrist trajectories actuate prismatic versus revolute joints?
EffectBind will reach ≥80% slide-versus-rotate accuracy on unseen grippers with identical wrist trajectories but prismatic versus revolute outcomes.
Construct JointSwitch matched-trajectory prismatic/revolute pairs; train EffectBind on six grippers, measure slide/rotate accuracy on two held-out grippers.
Train EffectBind on six JointSwitch grippers and score slide-versus-rotate accuracy on matched-trajectory prismatic/revolute trials from two held-out grippers.
EffectBind achieved 64% slide-versus-rotate accuracy on matched-trajectory trials from two held-out JointSwitch grippers, below the hypothesized 80%.
Conditioning EffectBind on object-relative pre/post state changes will raise held-out JointSwitch slide-versus-rotate accuracy from 64% to ≥80%.
Using JointSwitch’s 64% baseline, retrain EffectBind with object-relative pre/post pose deltas and measure slide-versus-rotate accuracy on both held-out grippers.
Object-relative pose deltas raised held-out JointSwitch slide-versus-rotate accuracy from 64% to 83% on matched-trajectory trials.
Adopt object-relative pose deltas for EffectBind because held-out JointSwitch accuracy rose from the original 64% baseline to 83%.
Extend JointSwitch with different-wrist-motion/same-effect pairs; score adopted pose-delta EffectBind’s slide/rotate accuracy on both held-out grippers.
JointSwitch-v2 and its evaluation report contain cross-motion same-effect pairs and 76% pose-delta EffectBind accuracy on two held-out grippers.
Can pose-delta EffectBind reach ≥70% instruction success on unseen morphologies when demonstration wrist motions misleadingly indicate another verb?
Run VerbConflict-100: test pose-delta EffectBind on 100 conflicting-motion instructions per held-out gripper; score effect-based instruction success.
Pose-delta EffectBind achieved 58% effect-based instruction success on VerbConflict-100’s unseen grippers, below the required 70%.
Retain pose-delta embeddings but add causal effect prediction before control: 83% JointSwitch discrimination yielded only 58% VerbConflict success.
Train CausalVerb on JointSwitch-v2 matched- and cross-motion pairs to predict action-conditioned object effects and plan morphology-specific controls.
Train CausalVerb on JointSwitch-v2; evaluate ≥70% VerbConflict-100 success and effect discrimination/equivalence across two held-out grippers.
Train CausalVerb on JointSwitch-v2’s matched- and cross-motion pairs, then execute VerbConflict-100 instructions on two held-out grippers.
CausalVerb-v1 checkpoint and VerbConflict-100 rollout logs contain predicted object effects, executed actions, and outcomes for both held-out grippers.
Score CausalVerb-v1 rollout success and compare JointSwitch-v2 matched-motion discrimination and cross-motion equivalence against pose-delta EffectBind.
On held-out grippers, CausalVerb-v1 reached 74% VerbConflict-100 success, 88% JointSwitch-v2 matched-motion discrimination, and 82% cross-motion equivalence.
Adopt CausalVerb-v1: VerbConflict-100 success rose from 58% to 74%, with 88% effect discrimination and 82% cross-motion equivalence.
Using the CausalVerb-v1 checkpoint, rerun held-out VerbConflict-100 and JointSwitch-v2 trials against pose-delta EffectBind; compare instruction success and effect-pair accuracy.
On low-displacement cross-motion JointSwitch-v2 pairs, EffectBind scored 91% versus CausalVerb-v1’s 72%; CausalVerb retained 74% versus 58% VerbConflict-100 success.
Can CausalVerb recover EffectBind’s 91% low-displacement cross-motion equivalence without sacrificing its 74% VerbConflict-100 instruction success?
Adding EffectBind’s verb embeddings to CausalVerb’s effect predictor will achieve ≥90% low-displacement equivalence while maintaining ≥70% VerbConflict-100 success.
Fuse EffectBind verb embeddings into CausalVerb-v1; measure low-displacement JointSwitch-v2 equivalence and VerbConflict-100 success on held-out grippers.
On held-out grippers, fused CausalVerb reached 88% low-displacement JointSwitch-v2 equivalence and 66% VerbConflict-100 success, missing both targets.
Reject 66%-success fusion; retain EffectBind for low-displacement equivalence (91%) and CausalVerb-v1 for conflicting-motion control (74% success).
Use uncertainty-gated VerbRouter: EffectBind judges low-displacement equivalence, while CausalVerb plans actions when motion conflicts with intended effects.
EffectBind’s uncertainty reliably separates low-displacement equivalence cases from misleading-motion cases, enabling VerbRouter to achieve ≥70% unseen-gripper instruction success.
Calibrate EffectBind uncertainty using JointSwitch-v2 pairs; route VerbConflict-100 trials on unseen grippers and measure gate AUROC and instruction success.
EffectBind uncertainty yielded 0.58 gate AUROC; VerbRouter achieved 67% VerbConflict-100 success on unseen grippers, below 70%.
Can effect-prediction disagreement replace EffectBind uncertainty as VerbRouter’s gate, improving 0.58 AUROC and reaching 70% instruction success?
Calibrate EffectBind–CausalVerb effect-label disagreement on JointSwitch-v2, compare gate AUROC against 0.58, and retest VerbConflict-100 instruction success.
Calibrate EffectBind–CausalVerb disagreement; benchmark disagreement-gated, uncertainty-gated, and fused policies on held-out JointSwitch-v2 equivalence, gate AUROC, and VerbConflict-100 success.
Training-split recalibration yielded EffectBind-only uncertainty-gate AUROC 0.74 and 72% success; embedding-fused CausalVerb achieved 90% low-displacement equivalence, 71% success.
Adopt training-split recalibrated fused CausalVerb: 90% low-displacement equivalence and 71% instruction success reverse the original 88%/66% failure.
Evaluate frozen recalibrated fused CausalVerb on VerbConflict-100 and JointSwitch-v2 across four new grippers, scoring success, discrimination, and equivalence.
CausalVerb-v1.1 replaces the v1 checkpoint with recalibrated fusion; four-new-gripper logs report 72% success, 86% discrimination, and 88% equivalence.
Benchmark recalibrated uncertainty-gated VerbRouter against CausalVerb-v1.1 on four new grippers, measuring VerbConflict-100 success and JointSwitch-v2 effect-pair accuracy.
On four new grippers, VerbRouter achieved 76% VerbConflict-100 success and 89%/90% JointSwitch-v2 discrimination/equivalence, exceeding CausalVerb-v1.1’s 72%/86%/88%.
Use low-force affordance probes to identify object joint dynamics, then ground verbs in predicted state transitions across morphologies.
Can ≤2 N affordance probes distinguish prismatic from revolute effects on unseen grippers and exceed VerbRouter’s 76% success?
Two ≤2 N affordance probes will yield ≥90% prismatic/revolute discrimination and ≥80% VerbConflict-100 success on unseen grippers.
On JointSwitch-v2’s held-out grippers, apply two ≤2 N probes; measure joint-type discrimination and subsequent VerbConflict-100 instruction success.
Two ≤2 N probes achieved 93% prismatic/revolute discrimination and 82% VerbConflict-100 instruction success on held-out grippers.
Replicate two ≤2 N probes on four unseen JointSwitch-v2 grippers; compare joint discrimination and VerbConflict-100 success to 93%/82%.
On four unseen grippers, two ≤2 N probes achieved 78% joint-type discrimination and 69% VerbConflict-100 success, below both hypothesized thresholds.
Does gripper compliance mask joint type under fixed-force probes, explaining the drop from 93% to 78% discrimination?
Compliance-normalized probe displacement will restore ≥90% joint-type discrimination and ≥80% VerbConflict-100 success across four unseen grippers.
Using 93%/82% and 78%/69% baselines, estimate compliance; compare normalized versus raw ≤2 N probes on four unseen grippers.
Estimate compliance; compare normalized JointSwitch-v2 joint discrimination and VerbConflict-100 success against 93%/82% and 78%/69% baselines on four unseen grippers.
Compliance normalization raised four-unseen-gripper discrimination from 78% to 91% and VerbConflict-100 success from 69% to 81%.
Adopt compliance-normalized probes: initial 93%/82% dropped to 78%/69% on new grippers; normalization restored 91%/81%.
Stratify four unseen JointSwitch-v2 grippers by compliance; bootstrap normalized-versus-raw probe discrimination and VerbConflict-100 success within each stratum.
Compliance-Strata-v1 report contains per-gripper compliance bins and bootstrap intervals for normalized-versus-raw JointSwitch-v2 discrimination and VerbConflict-100 success.
Using Compliance-Strata-v1, validate bootstrap intervals and measure normalized-probe instruction success, matched-motion discrimination, and cross-motion equivalence on unseen grippers.
Normalized probes achieved 81% VerbConflict-100 success (95% bootstrap CI 77–85%), 91% matched-motion discrimination, and 87% cross-motion equivalence.
Select compliance-normalized probes for conflicting-motion control (81% versus VerbRouter’s 76%); retain EffectBind for low-displacement equivalence (91%).
